title: Choose the notes page layout
question: How should the Discrete Structure reading page be arranged?

options.label: Projected Outline & Transcript
options.lineage: lecture outline projected beside a transcript
options.thesis: A numbered chapter outline on the left, a calm reading column on the right.
options.viewport: Masthead at top with brand and breadcrumb. Left rail lists six chapters as a numbered syllabus. Right column opens on the selected chapter with a readable measure and one highlighted slide number in the margin.
options.risk: The outline can feel like navigation chrome if chapter labels are too quiet.

options.label: Lecture Slide Tabs
options.lineage: projected slide deck with tabbed chapters
options.thesis: Six numbered slide tabs run across the top; one reading pane holds the open chapter.
options.viewport: Masthead above a horizontal row of six chapter tabs. The active tab is lit yellow. Below, a single reading column carries the chapter title, opening paragraph, and a definition callout.
options.risk: Tabs compete with the reading column when the chapter names wrap.

options.label: Index-Card Stack
options.lineage: numbered index cards on a lecture desk
options.thesis: Six chapter cards sit in a row; the open card expands into the reading surface.
options.viewport: Masthead, then a row of six small numbered cards with taped tabs. Beneath them, the active card opens into a wide reading panel with a chapter list and an example block.
options.risk: Cards can turn the page into a gallery instead of a document.
